# Saffra (Mirrowen): Side-Activity Menu (SEALED — DM ONLY)

> **Saffra** (aka Safra, Saffrah). The tabaxi trade city on the Rennet's mid-course: bright awnings, bells and story-halls. Mirrors Tollhaven.
> **Government:** an **elected Tale-Keeper**, the best storyteller, chosen by audience acclaim at the **Great Telling** each year. **Tale-Keeper: Saffi-of-the-Lamplight** (NPC-061), who collects stories about "the boy who hears" and is an information broker and ally. **Law:** the **Tale-Keepers' truce**: inside Saffra's bell-ring, no one may draw a weapon on a story-night. Otherwise, the bell-wardens (tabaxi watchmen with long hooked poles) keep order and are bribable with a good anecdote.
> **When visited:** Ch14 (`chapters/act3/ch14.md`: the parley at the Great Telling; its side window has the Great Telling chain, bell-market haggling, the rooftop chase race with **Zuri Far-Wander**, and cat's-cradle duels). Mentioned in Ch9 (the Varga gate surfaces under Saffra's **Hall of Bells**). **Tier: T3.**
> **The chapter wins.** This file adds the shops, the Scratch (Saffra's sparring ring), odd jobs, stealing, the fence, and Saffra by act. Neutral, trading with everyone to survive, sheltering refugees in secret (`world/05`).

---

## 1. The city at a glance

- **Look:** a river city of red and saffron awnings stretched between towers; bells on every eave (thousands, all tuned, each family's its own note); story-halls with round doors; rooftops that are a second city (tabaxi walk them more than the streets); the **Hall of Bells**, with its flooded counting-house mirror below (the Varga gate's far side).
- **Sound:** bells, always; haggling in a sing-song; a story being told somewhere, always, with an audience gasping.
- **Feel:** curious about everything; a city that pays for stories. Tabaxi know more about Eyrland than anyone in Mirrowen. They're delighted by Ash. They want to touch Bart (Bart permits this, for a fee).
- **The currency of Saffra:** coin works, but **a new story** is worth a meal anywhere, and **a true story nobody's heard** is worth a night's lodging. Ash and Zeke can eat for free all week.

---

## 2. Shops and services (the bell-market)

Bell-market haggling: Ch14 (**Persuasion or Deception vs the trader's Insight +6; win by 5+: 20% off**). Saffra sells potions and charms at book price.

### 2.1 Copper-Whisker's Charms (the bell-market)
**Keeper: Yesh Copper-Whisker** (NPC-353; aka Yesh Copperwhisker), a plump, elderly tabaxi with a copper-dyed whisker on each side, who sells **song-charms** (Mirrowen's magic runs on song, `world/05`) and gossips in exchange for gossip.
**Interior (painter):** a stall that's more of a tent of bells: hundreds of tiny bells and woven song-knots hanging at every height; cushions; a brass teapot; a sleeping kitten in a basket of charms.
| Item | Rarity | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Song-knot** (a woven charm that holds one note; hum it and the knot glows; a light-source that doesn't use glimmer) | Common | 100 gp | Lark wants one in every color |
| **Potion of Greater Healing** · **Superior Healing** | Uncommon / Rare consumable | 200 / 2,000 gp | Mirrowen-brewed (herbal, sweet) |
| **Bell of Waking** (a small bell; ring it as an action: a Hushed creature within 30 ft has **disadvantage** on its next save against being woken) | Uncommon (Mirrowen) | 400 gp | ×3. **Vital** for Ch15–16's waking chains (gives advantage on one Performance check to wake). |
| **Chime of Opening** | Rare | 4,000 gp | |
| **Instrument of the Bards** (a tabaxi lute, *Doss Lute*) | Uncommon | 400 gp | |
| **Pipes of Haunting** | Uncommon | 400 gp | |
| **Hat of the Story-Teller** (*Cap of Water Breathing*'s cousin: advantage on Performance to tell a story, once a day) | Uncommon (Mirrowen) | 400 gp | For the Great Telling |
| **Ioun Stone (Awareness)** | Rare | 4,000 gp | "From the Tall Folk side. Fell out of the counting-house pool. Three of them have, over the years." |

### 2.2 The Long Shelf (story-hall bookshop)
**Keeper: Lio-of-the-Long-Shelf** (NPC-354; aka Leo, Lio Longshelf), a thin, elegant, nearsighted tabaxi archivist who sells books by the story, not the page. **Spell scrolls** (Mirrowen song-scrolls; work as normal scrolls), 4th–6th level, at Rare/Very Rare consumable prices. The **Sundering, from Mirrowen's side**: a book of tellings Zeke would give his teeth for (300 gp; or a story Lio hasn't heard). **Gives advantage** on History or Arcana about the Sundering for the rest of the campaign.

### 2.3 Lodging and food
Every story-hall has rooms. A night: **one story** (Charisma (Performance) DC 13), or 5 sp. Tabaxi street food: grilled river-fish with honey and pepper, 1 sp.

## 3. Festivals and contests

- **The Great Telling** (Mirrowen's Thawing): **Ch14 runs it** (the chain at DC 17 / 19 / 21; the parley happens under its truce). The year's Tale-Keeper is chosen by acclaim. **If Ash wins it**, he's offered the Keepership (he can't keep it; Saffi laughs and keeps it for him "until you come back to tell the end").
- **The rooftop chase race** (Ch14): Athletics or Acrobatics DC 17 / 19 / 21, advantage with Ash's climb speed. **Zuri Far-Wander** (Tier 3) is fast and rude. 300 gp purse; Zuri carries a message anywhere in Mirrowen, once.
- **Cat's-cradle duels** (Ch14): Sleight of Hand contested (tabaxi +8), best of three.
- **Bell-Ringing Eve** (any new moon): every family rings its own note in turn at dusk. Visitors are given a bell and asked to find their note. **Wisdom (Perception) DC 15** to hear which note in the city is "missing" (one family's gone still). It's a quiet beat and a quest hook (§6 job 2).

---


### Skill contests (`00-index.md` §11; CHG-21)
- **The Awning Run** (Gauntlet, Hard, T3): over the bright awnings and up the bell-ropes of the Hall of Bells. Tabaxi (+10 climb and jump) usually win. Climb speed: advantage on every climb. **Entry 50 gp, pot; the Tale-Keepers take 10%** and a story about every passer.
- **The Tumbling** (judged, T3): three passes (**Acrobatics DC 16**, a knife-catch **Dex save DC 17**, a finale in **Performance**). Prize: **the crowd's hat (2d6 × 25 gp)** and a line in the Great Telling, which in Saffra is worth more.
- (Ch14's rooftop chase race with Zuri Far-Wander is its own scene; run it as a **Rooftop Race**, §11.6.)

### New contests (`00-index.md` §12–13; CHG-22)
- **Strange Arms: the Far Booth** (circuit stop 4): Mirrowen's weapons (#12, 13, 14) arrive, plus one Eyrland weapon for the tabaxi to fumble. Pashi Two-Rivers (NPC-102) joins.
- **Patter Night: the Small Telling.** Tabaxi judge the story, not the coins (tabaxi +8).


## 4. The Scratch (sparring ring)

**Ring formats (`00-index.md` §5.1, CHG-19):** the Scratch is tabaxi **Touches** with padded claws (a claw-touch counts like a waster hit; tabaxi ring AC 15–16). Outsiders may ask for **Ring-Out on the bell-rope beam**. No magic in any format: no smites, no spells, no Wild Shape, no familiars. Dexterity fighters can win here.

A sanded courtyard behind the Hall of Bells where tabaxi spar with **padded claws**. Ring rules (`00-index.md` §5), three rounds, nonlethal. **No weapons at all** (Ash fights unarmed; Sneak Attack doesn't apply unless he has a way, which he doesn't). Purses (T3): 150 / 200–400 / 750 gp. It's fast, flashy and funny.

### SCRATCH-CHAMPION (a tabaxi sparrer)
*Medium Humanoid (tabaxi), Chaotic Good* · **AC** 17 · **Initiative** +6 · **HP** 79 · **Speed** 40 ft., climb 30 ft. · **CR** 8 (PB +3)
*Tuned for party level 14 (Ash alone; ring DPR 26, HP 101).*
- ***Feline Agility.*** Once per bout, double speed for a turn.
- ***Multiattack.*** Three Padded Claw strikes: *Melee* +9, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 1d10 + 5 bludgeoning, nonlethal.
- ***Pounce (bonus action, after moving 20 ft straight).*** **DC 16 Str save** or prone.
- ***Round-2 Turn: "Up the Wall."*** She runs up the courtyard wall and drops on Ash: advantage on the next attack; Ash can't make opportunity attacks against her this round.
- ***Reaction: Twist Away.*** When hit, move 10 ft without provoking (once per round).

---

## 5. Street fights

Under the truce: none on story-nights. Otherwise, rooftop scuffles. **Local trick: the awnings.** A creature shoved off a roof lands on an awning (**DC 15 Dex save**: on a success it bounces safely to the street; on a failure it tears through for 2d6). The bell-wardens hook people off roofs with long poles; anyone hooked is out.

---

## 6. Odd jobs

| d6 | Job | Pay (T3) | Quick run |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Carry a sealed story (a letter) from Saffi to Grandmother Umbari in Tuskhold through the siege lines | Saffi's favor (★-route material for Ch14–16) | Stealth DC 18 ×2, Deception DC 17 at a Horned checkpoint |
| 2 | Find the family whose bell went silent (§3) | 300 gp (the bell-market's collection) | Investigation DC 17; they're Hushed in their own house, sitting together; wake them (DC 19) |
| 3 | Guard a refugee raft leaving at night for the Free Clans | 200 gp | An ordinary fight on the river with a Horned patrol (use the Act III Horned soldier blocks) |
| 4 | Buy back a stolen Warren Mothers' songbook from a trader who doesn't know what it is (`world/05` "things worth stealing") | Mother Burdock's gratitude | Persuasion DC 17 (he wants a better story for it); or steal it (Medium security) |
| 5 | Recover three Ioun stones that "fell out of the counting-house pool" before a Horned officer buys them | one stone (Awareness) | Sleight of Hand DC 18 at the bell-market |
| 6 | Be the subject of a story: let a young tabaxi teller follow the party for a day and tell it that night | 100 gp and the city's love | No roll. It's wonderful, wildly inaccurate, and Bart is the hero. |

## 7. Things worth stealing

`world/05`: **Brannoc's orders** (carried by Horned couriers through Saffra; High security on the courier), the **keys of the Quiet Pens** (not here; at Cairn Answer), a **stolen Warren Mothers' songbook** (job 4).
| Target | Where | Security | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A Horned courier's dispatch case | a story-hall where he's drinking | High (DC 17) | none: orders and troop counts | Ch14–15 intel; the chapter wins if it uses it |
| The Tale-Keeper's **Book of Endings** (every year's winning tale) | Saffi's study | Very High | — | Don't. Saffi would show it to him if he asked. (She would. She's been waiting for him to ask.) |
**Fence: Yesh Copper-Whisker** (NPC-353) at **40%**, or for a story.

## 8. Rivals

- **Zuri Far-Wander** (Tier 3): the fast, rude rooftop champion (Ch14).
- **A rival teller, Pim-of-the-Seven-Lies** (Tier 3, no ID): enters the Great Telling every year with the same story (badly), and is the city's most beloved loser.

| When | What it's like |
|---|---|
| **Before Ch14** | Neutral, trading with Brannoc to survive, hiding refugees. Prices **+20%** (wartime). |
